As blood travels through the body via the arteries, the arteries get smaller in diameter until they terminate into 
arterioles, the smallest arteries. These arterioles link with capillaries and then connect to venules, the smallest 
veins (Gupta and Shea, 2022). Capillaries are thin-walled vessels that connect arterioles and venules. As shown in 
Figure 11.6, they are the vehicle for the final exchange of oxygen and nutrients into tissues and wastes into the 
blood (Gupta & Shea, 2022).
